episode.title: Newton the Alchemist. Gandhi the Black Swan

chapters.title: Introduction: Ajay is an escaped convict
Chapter 1: Isaac Newton -- The Last of the Magicians
Chapter 2: Mohandas Gandhi -- A Black Swan Event?

episode.tagline: Isaac Newton was not just a great scientist, but the last of the magicians. Mohandas Gandhi was a black swan event: a flawed, complex man who shaped history.
episode.about: In this episode, Ajay talks about Isaac Newton, and why he was a product of historical forces. Amit cites Mohandas Gandhi as an example of why historical currents aren't everything, and historical accidents can produce a man like Gandhi who changes everything. Ajay and Amit also recommend some of their favourite books -- and one outstanding bookshop.

Ajay slips and says 'Newton showed up at the auction.' Amit corrects him to Keynes, and Ajay replies: 'Would be nice if Newton showed up.'

Newton's million words on alchemy: 'That's like the Robert Caro book without the 200,000 words on Jane Jacobs taken out' — a nod to The…
Epicycles, the 'wheels within wheels' that kept orbits circular: Ajay notes this is where the phrase comes from.
Alexander Pope's epitaph, as quoted: 'Nature and her mysteries lay hidden in the night. God said, Let Newton be and all was light.'
Asked how gravity actually works, Newton replied 'I do not make hypotheses' — which Ajay translates into modern English as 'I do not…
Nehru's line, cited by Ajay, that he is a battlefield inside which many ideas compete for supremacy, applied to Newton and to all of us.
Amit recounts their dinner argument about free will: Amit said there can't be any, Ajay said of course there is, and Amit concluded 'we…
Carlyle's Great Man Theory of History, which Amit notes was named that because in Carlyle's day only men were seen as agents of history.
Keir Hardie's line, as Amit recalls it, on the Congress: the moderates are extreme in their moderation and the extremists are moderate…
VS Naipaul's remark that Gandhi was 'the least Indian of the Indian leaders.'

Gandhi, asked by a journalist what he thought of Western civilisation: 'It would be a good idea.'

The 'Amar Chitra Katha story' of independence: the Congress fought the British and we got freedom. Both hosts push back on it.
Ajay's contemporary analogy for Europe's self-destruction helping Indian independence: 'If Wagner and Russian forces are going to fight…
Gandhi and Kallenbach called each other 'upper house' and 'lower house', possibly because one decided spending and the other had a veto.…
Amit on Keynes's most famous line: 'In the long run, we are all dead. So, which of course is undoubtedly true as well.'
